title.en: A craft that chooses its maker

text.en: In some villages, a craft such as pot making passes from mother to daughter. What happens when the daughter cannot seem to learn it? This story from Nagaland shows how skills are really passed on.

Sentila's mother, Arenla, is an expert pot maker. The work is tiring: digging clay from the riverbank, carrying it uphill and pounding it, for only a few rupees.
Arenla felt Sentila should learn weaving instead because it is cleaner, can be done indoors and earns more. Yet Sentila kept visiting the potters, fascinated by how a shapeless lump became a pot.
Village gossip began, and the village council summoned Sentila's father Mesoba. The elders reminded him that skills like pot making belong to the community and must be passed on.
Arenla finally taught Sentila to dig clay and soak and pound it, but for almost a year Sentila could not shape even one pot and felt shame and frustration.
When Sentila matured, she stayed in a girls' dormitory under a kind widow called Onula, who noticed that Sentila was too tense and showed her how to shape a pot.
With new confidence Sentila made a pot. Onula told her to watch how her mother shaped the mouth of the pot.
On a sunny day Arenla left Sentila alone with a headache as an excuse. Sentila made pot after pot, almost matching her mother's tally.
She returned and found her mother dead. After the funeral Onula saw two rows of pots in the shed, one by the mother and one by the daughter, and felt a new pot maker was born.

problem.en: Why did Arenla at first discourage Sentila from pot making?

text.en: The work is hard and badly paid.
Weaving earns more and is easier.
So she wished a better life for her daughter.

prompt.en: Explain how Sentila finally learned pot making.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking skill comes only from one's own parent

points.en: Crafts are passed on within communities.
Sentila learned through patience, watching and a helper.
Hard work needs encouragement and confidence.
A new generation continues a tradition.
